The story of the Paralyzed Man at the Pool of Bethesda — a man who had been unable to walk for thirty-eight years encounters Jesus, who asks him a surprisingly personal question and then does the unexpected.

The story of Joseph — a favored son sold into slavery by his own brothers, who endures betrayal, false accusation, and years in prison, yet rises to save the very people who wronged him, revealing how God can weave suffering into purpose.
Elijah, exhausted and convinced he is utterly alone after fleeing for his life, is met by God not in thunder or fire, but in a gentle whisper — and is tenderly restored and recommissioned.
The Prodigal Son — a young man who demands his inheritance early, wastes it all, and finally comes to his senses and returns home, only to be met by a father who was already running toward him.
David, a young shepherd boy armed with nothing but a sling and unwavering faith, steps forward to face the giant Goliath when every trained soldier in Israel has backed away in fear.
The story of Daniel in the lions' den — a man of unwavering prayer who refused to hide his faith even when a death sentence hung over him, and how God shut the mouths of the lions.
The story of Ruth — a young Moabite widow who chose loyalty over security, followed her mother-in-law into a foreign land, and discovered that faithful love is never wasted or unseen.
The story of the Good Samaritan — a parable Jesus told about a man left for dead on a dangerous road, and the unlikely stranger who stopped to help him when everyone else walked by.
The story of Esther — a young Jewish woman who found herself queen of Persia at just the right moment, and had to decide whether to risk everything to save her people from destruction.

The story of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego — three young men who refused to bow to a king's golden idol and were thrown into a blazing furnace, only for a mysterious fourth figure to appear walking beside them in the flames.
The story of Jonah — a prophet who ran in the opposite direction from God's call, discovered there is no outrunning divine purpose, and learned that God's mercy reaches further than any of us expect.
The story of Mary and Martha — two sisters who both loved Jesus, yet responded to his presence in opposite ways, and what Jesus gently revealed about what matters most.

The story of the Prodigal Son's older brother — a loyal son who stayed home, worked faithfully, and yet found his heart was further from his father than he realized when grace was shown to his wayward brother.
The story of the Ten Lepers — ten men healed by Jesus, yet only one turns back to say thank you, revealing something profound about gratitude, faith, and what it means to be truly whole.
Peter walks on water toward Jesus in the middle of a storm — and what happens when his eyes move from Jesus to the waves around him reveals something deeply human about faith and fear.
Zacchaeus, a despised tax collector, climbs a tree just to catch a glimpse of Jesus — and ends up with an encounter that changes his entire life.

The story of the Road to Emmaus — two disciples walking away from Jerusalem in grief and confusion on the day of the resurrection, joined by a stranger who opens the Scriptures to them, and how they finally recognize him in the breaking of bread.

The story of Gideon — a man hiding in fear who is called "mighty warrior" by an angel, and who learns that God deliberately strips away every human advantage so that victory can belong to no one but God.

The story of the Wedding at Cana — where Mary brings an embarrassing problem to Jesus, he performs his first recorded miracle by turning water into wine, and a small moment of trust quietly changes everything.
The story of the Tower of Babel — humanity, united in pride, attempts to build a monument to their own greatness, and God quietly scatters what human ambition tried to cement together.
The story of Moses and the burning bush — a shepherd in exile who felt forgotten and unqualified, called by God from an unexpected place to do the impossible.

The story of Noah — a man who trusted God's word and built an ark when there was no rain in sight, and how faithful obedience carried him and his family through an overwhelming flood into a brand-new beginning.

Joseph's brothers sell him into slavery out of jealousy, yet through years of suffering, false accusation, and imprisonment, God quietly works a purpose that eventually saves an entire nation — and leads to a moment of breathtaking forgiveness.

The story of the Feeding of the Five Thousand — a young boy offers his small lunch of five loaves and two fish to Jesus, and what happens next shows that nothing given willingly into God's hands is ever too little.

The story of Elijah under the juniper tree — a mighty prophet who collapses in exhaustion and despair after a great victory, and how God meets him not with rebuke, but with rest, food, and gentle presence.

The story of David and Goliath — a young shepherd boy steps onto a battlefield to face a giant that had terrified an entire army, armed with nothing but a sling, five stones, and unshakeable trust in God.
Daniel is thrown into a den of lions for refusing to stop praying to God, and emerges the next morning completely unharmed — a story about quiet, unshakeable faith in the face of real consequences.

The story of Ruth — a young widow from Moab who chose loyalty over safety, left everything she knew to follow her grieving mother-in-law back to Bethlehem, and discovered that faithfulness and kindness have a way of being quietly rewarded.

The story of the Good Samaritan — a man beaten and left for dying on the road to Jericho, passed over by the respectable and religious, until an unexpected outsider stops and shows what love for a neighbor truly looks like.

Esther, a young Jewish woman living in exile, risks her life by approaching the king uninvited to save her people from a plot to destroy them — discovering that she was placed in her position for exactly such a moment.

The story of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego — three young men who refused to bow to a king's golden statue and were thrown into a furnace so hot it killed the soldiers who threw them in, yet walked out completely unharmed — and were not alone inside.

The story of Jonah — a prophet who ran from God's call, was swallowed by a great fish, and discovered that there is no place far enough to escape God's mercy, neither for himself nor for the people he least wanted to love.

The story of Mary and Martha — two sisters who both love Jesus, yet reveal two very different postures of the heart when he visits their home, leading to a gentle but profound lesson about what it means to truly sit with what matters most.

The story of the Prodigal Son — a young man who demands his inheritance early, wastes everything, hits rock bottom, and finally comes home to a father who has been watching and waiting — revealing a picture of grace that is almost too generous to believe.

The story of the Paralyzed Man at the Pool of Bethesda — a man who had been unable to walk for 38 years encounters Jesus beside a crowded pool, and a single unexpected question cuts straight to the heart of what it means to want to be made whole.

The story of the Transfiguration — Jesus takes three of his closest disciples up a mountain, where his appearance is suddenly transformed in dazzling light, Moses and Elijah appear beside him, and a voice from a cloud declares who Jesus truly is.
The story of Zacchaeus — a despised tax collector who climbed a tree just to catch a glimpse of Jesus, and found that the one he was trying to see had already seen him.

The story of the woman at the well — a Samaritan woman who came to draw water alone in the heat of the day and found herself in a conversation with Jesus that knew everything about her and offered her something no well could ever hold.
The story of Peter walking on water — a fisherman who stepped out of a boat in the middle of a storm at Jesus's invitation, and what happened when his eyes moved from Jesus to the waves around him.
The story of Gideon — a man who felt weak, small, and unqualified, yet was called by God to lead a victory so lopsided that no one could take the credit except God himself.
The story of the Lost Sheep — Jesus describes a shepherd who leaves ninety-nine sheep to search for the one that wandered away, revealing how precious every single person is to God.

The story of the Armor of God in Ephesians 6 — Paul describes a spiritual battle invisible to the eye and invites believers to stand firm by putting on truth, righteousness, faith, and the word of God as their daily protection.
The story of Noah's Ark — a man who trusted God's word and built a boat on dry land, saving his family and the animals when the flood came, and the rainbow covenant God made afterward.

The story of Joseph and his coat of many colors — a favored son sold into slavery by his own brothers who rises, through years of hardship and faithfulness, to a position where he can save the very people who betrayed him, revealing that what others meant for harm, God was weaving into something greater.

The story of the Ten Lepers — ten men healed by Jesus in an instant, yet only one turns back to say thank you, revealing something profound about gratitude, faith, and what it means to truly receive a gift.
The story of Elijah under the juniper tree — a burned-out prophet who wanted to give up, and the surprising, gentle way God met him in his exhaustion.

The story of David and Goliath — a young shepherd boy faces a terrifying giant warrior when no soldier in Israel's army dares to step forward, armed with nothing but a sling, five smooth stones, and an unshakeable trust in God.
The story of Daniel in the lions' den — a faithful man who refused to stop praying even when it was made illegal, was thrown into a pit of lions, and walked out the next morning without a scratch.

The story of Ruth and Naomi — a young Moabite widow who chose to stay with her grieving mother-in-law and journey to a foreign land, whose quiet faithfulness and loyal love led to restoration neither of them could have imagined.

The story of the Road to Emmaus — two grieving disciples walking away from Jerusalem on the day of the resurrection encounter a stranger who opens the scriptures to them along the way, and only recognize him in a breathtaking moment at the dinner table.
The story of the Feeding of the Five Thousand — a massive hungry crowd, one boy's small lunch, and what Jesus did with it that left everyone astonished and twelve baskets left over.

The story of Esther — a young Jewish woman who became queen in a foreign land and risked everything to save her people from destruction, discovering that she had been placed exactly where she was for such a moment as this.

The story of the Prodigal Son's older brother — a faithful son who stayed home, worked hard, and struggled to rejoice when his wayward brother was welcomed back with celebration, revealing how resentment and a sense of fairness can quietly close the heart to grace.

The story of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego — three young men who refused to bow to a king's golden statue, were thrown into a furnace heated beyond imagination, and walked out unharmed, with a mysterious fourth figure seen walking beside them in the fire.

The story of Mary and Martha — two sisters who loved Jesus, but whose different responses to his visit reveal something timeless about busyness, presence, and what it means to sit at the feet of someone worth listening to.

The story of Jonah — a prophet who ran from God's call, was swallowed by a great fish, and discovered that God's mercy reaches further than any of us expect — including to the very people we'd rather not forgive.

The story of the Good Samaritan — a traveler left for dead on a dangerous road, passed by those who should have helped, until a stranger from a despised people stopped, cared, and paid the price himself, redefining what it truly means to love your neighbor.
The story of Zacchaeus — a wealthy, despised tax collector who climbed a tree just to catch a glimpse of Jesus, and found that Jesus had already spotted him — and wanted to come to his home.

The story of the Burning Bush — Moses, a shepherd in exile who felt disqualified by his past, encounters the living God in an ordinary desert bush that would not stop burning, and is called back to set his people free.

The story of the Wedding at Cana — Jesus performs his first recorded miracle at a wedding feast, quietly turning water into wine at his mother Mary's request, revealing both his glory and the abundant, unexpected nature of God's provision.
